what_happened: The job was meant to reclaim the build directories of interrupted jobs and check free disk before the producer runs. It was rejected at the final verdict. One of 7 acceptance criteria was unmet: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` must all pass. There was one major finding: behavior criterion 4 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). The event does not list any failed checks, so the stored fields do not say which of the three commands failed, or whether any did. The other 6 criteria were met.
cause: Nothing during the job requires the full gate (fmt, clippy, test) to be run and its output recorded before the final verdict. Nothing requires each behavior criterion to be tied to a command that actually ran. The producer can finish with the gate unrun or its evidence uncited, and only the final verifier compares evidence with criteria. At that point rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the plan, the checks or the producer's report.
prevention: Add a pre-verdict step in code. Before the verifier runs, Athena runs the repo gate (fmt, clippy, test) itself and records the exact commands and exit codes. It also checks that every behavior criterion has a demonstration that names a command in that record. If the gate fails or a criterion has no cited command, the job goes back to the producer with the specific gap, so it is fixed while the producer can still act and not rejected at the end.
proposed_request: Before the verifier runs, make Athena run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` itself and record each command with its exit code. Then check that every behavior criterion's evidence cites a command in that record. Accept this when: (1) a job whose gate fails is sent back to the producer with the failing command and output, not sent to the verifier; (2) a job where a behavior criterion cites no recorded command is sent back naming that criterion; (3) a job that passes both goes on to the verifier unchanged; (4) a test shows each of the three cases. Then re-ask the interrupted-job build-dir reclaim and pre-producer disk gate job, with criterion 4's evidence required to cite the commands that ran.
